title: Plugin Split QA
eyebrow: QA · steps 1 to 3 of the plugin split (#438, #439, #440) in draft pull request #452

short.lead: Steps 1 to 3 of the plugin split are built, and five of the six checks you asked for before any merge have passed. Existing behaviour is unchanged. Main's house-rules 2.74.2 and this branch gave the same result for 49 of the 64 recorded hook inputs, and each of the other 15 differs because of a change you approved. What is new: house-rules 2.75.0, the house-lib library and the rule-enforcement plugin. The sixth check is your QA, and one part of it has not been done: everything ran on Linux, but your PC runs Windows, which is where the 2.74.0 restructure broke. Choice 1 below asks how to check Windows before you pass QA.
short.hint: Tap a check for its evidence.
items: 1. Every test suite passes, here and in CI

Here: house-rules verify.py 941 checks, rule-enforcement 100, tools 70, the check that every house-lib copy matches its source and the check that each changed plugin's version was raised all pass. CI: the first run failed one test that read this repo's own files; it was fixed in commit 8e78ff7, and every run since has passed.

tools/replay_hooks.py fed 64 recorded hook inputs through main and through this branch. 15 differ, and each traces to an approved change. It also found a real bug that main has too: the command splitter ignored quotes, so a sed -i inside a quoted command slipped past a lock. Commit f92fd63 fixes it. Report: docs/plans/2026-11-02-plugin-split-replay.md.
The same real session (read, doc edit, source edit, a shell command, a helper, a commit, a reply) ran on main and on this branch. Neither refused anything, and both ended in success.

In a fresh config, the marketplace added from GitHub's copy of this branch installed house-lib 0.1.0, rule-enforcement 0.1.0 and house-rules 2.75.0. A session on that install read a file with no refusal, and the rules loaded once.
On a throwaway copy of main, merging this branch and then running git revert -m 1 on the merge left files identical to main. After a real merge, the same one command undoes it.

Nothing here ran on Windows. Your PC was recorded on 2026-10-28 as Windows 11 with PowerShell 5.1 and Python 3.13.7. That record comes from a check run on your PC that day and was not confirmed today.

changes: Shared plumbing with no hooks of its own, copied into each plugin by tools/sync_library.py; CI fails if a copy drifts.
Loads the rules at session start, sends them to helpers, adds the per-message reminder, and holds the repeat-failure lock.
Before: house-rules loaded the rules itself, and each of four end-of-reply checks blocked once, then let the next reply through.
A failing end-of-reply check blocks up to three times, then source edits and commits are refused until it passes. The action that fixes the check is always allowed.
Step 3 (#440), part A (rule loading moved) and part B (the repeat-failure lock).
Loses the rule-loading hooks and 19 of its 21 switches that turned a check off.
21 HOUSE_RULES_ switches could turn a check off.
19 of the 21 are gone. The permission timer, the 20th, loses only its off setting, and the helper-record switch, the 21st, stays, as you asked.
Step 3 (#440), part C (the off switches removed).
choices: Choice 1: how does the Windows check happen before you pass QA?
Connect your PC, and I run it

In the Claude desktop app on your PC, turn on Remote Control under Settings, Claude Code, Remote Control, and add your AjsClaudeCodeTools folder. Then tell me here, and I ask to use that folder. I then install the branch's plugins into a throwaway config there and run the same checks, in your shell.
Pass QA without a Windows check
The risk is the one that sank 2.74.0: a fault that only shows on Windows reaches main. Rolling back is one tested command.
Whichever you pick, nothing merges until you pass QA.
